A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adam-mini research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v6 reports original optimization experiments, LLM pre-training and alignment results, throughput measurements, and vision and graph experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v7 retains original empirical results and adds Transformer motivation experiments, aggregation ablations, and further vision training and image-quality evaluations.

M1.justification: The blockwise second-moment averaging update, momentum, weight decay, and architecture-specific partition rules remain unchanged. v7's general-form Algorithm 1 restates the existing procedure; Appendix B retains the implementation and partition algorithms.

E1.justification: Figure 3 replaces synthetic binary-classification data with CIFAR-100. Appendix D.5 adds ImageNet image generation through DiT-XL-2 and DC-AE-Diffusion, extending the earlier CelebA generation coverage. The main language, alignment, classification, and graph tasks remain. Adding Swin to existing ImageNet classification changes model coverage rather than the task itself.

E2.justification: Figure 13(b) adds AdamW to the Adafactor comparison. New Figure 14 compares blockwise GD with Adam-mini and a baseline labeled Adam, although its caption says AdamW. Lion's reported Llama 2-1B comparison is removed and a GPT-2-125M comparison is added (v6 Figure 16 versus v7 Figure 20). The principal comparator set remains stable.

E3.justification: v7 introduces additional vision model configurations and FID/Inception Score evaluation, revises Lion's model and hyperparameter sweeps, and replaces Figure 3's 10-neuron, 500-step setup with an 8-neuron MLP trained for 20 epochs. Llama 3-8B's stated learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 3e-4, and ResNet accuracy is relabeled from test to validation. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Figure 7's checkpoint description also changes to one step in the prose while its caption retains 1%.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.1 tests Adam's preconditioning on actual Transformer Hessian blocks and evaluates grid-searched blockwise GD on a one-layer Transformer. Appendix D.2 directly compares mean(v) with 1-norm, 2-norm, maximum, and minimum alternatives. The revised Lion analysis further investigates tuning and instability. These substantially expand tests of the method's motivation and design.

E5.justification: The shared-seed trajectory comparison and Figure 5's averaging over 100 initial points and 40 sampled rotations remain unchanged. v7 adds no repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v7 adds condition-number, aggregation-ablation, and vision results. New Table 7 reports DiT-XL-2 FID of 91.83 for AdamW and 88.20 for Adam-mini. Figure 3 and the Lion results are replaced under revised settings; the appendix Llama 2-1B Adam-mini loss curve also changes (v6 Figure 14 versus v7 Figure 16). Section 2.3 changes the stated Hessian magnitude ratio from 10^5 to 10^6. Headline efficiency, MT-Bench, and final scaling-perplexity table values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Hessian derivative moves from v6 Equation 1 to v7 Appendix C, Equation 3, with equivalent notation. The partition principle, preconditioner definitions, and mathematical reasoning are retained. The new condition-number comparisons are empirical, and no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: Hessian-guided partitioning removes at least 99.9% of second-moment learning-rate entries, approximately halves optimizer memory, and preserves competitive performance while improving throughput. The added experiments support these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly qualifies the Hessian argument as informal and expands the rationale for averaging v. Section 3.2 adds an interpretation concerning cheaper scaling-law studies. Appendix D.8 adds arguments about limited transferability of Lion tuning and Adam-mini's interpretability. These refine explanations and qualifications while retaining the main interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix F adds implementation references and learning rates for Swin, DiT-XL-2, and DC-AE-Diffusion. Appendix D.8 documents revised Lion search grids, and the CIFAR-100 configuration replaces the synthetic-data setup and generator. The Adam-mini repository link, hardware disclosures, and most existing training instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v7 adds citations for Swin, DiT, DC-AE, and the concurrent Deconstructing What Makes a Good Optimizer for Language Models study. The latter motivates an expanded comparison with Lion concerning tuning transfer and interpretability. Appendix A's broader research positioning remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains intact, with localized method rewrites distinguishing general and architecture-specific forms. The Hessian derivation and averaging discussion move into Appendix C, MT-Bench material moves into the experimental appendix, and the Lion subsection is extensively rewritten. Conference headers, acknowledgements, and broader-impact text are added.

P2.justification: v7 adds plots for Transformer motivation, aggregation ablations, and vision training, plus condition-number and image-quality tables. It replaces Figure 3's heatmaps, expands the non-LLM table, restructures the Lion figure, and revises the appendix scaling plot. General-form pseudocode appears in the main text, while the MT-Bench table moves to the appendix. These substantially change the displayed evidence.

improvement.justification: Compared with v6's intuitive justification for averaging v, v7 provides direct alternative-aggregation tests and additional Transformer-specific checks. Image-quality metrics strengthen the earlier diffusion evaluation, and explicitly calling the Hessian argument informal improves qualification. These are useful, incremental gains beyond the retained headline evidence. Their value is tempered by limited experimental detail and new inconsistencies, including duplicate Algorithm 3 labels, conflicting Figure 7 checkpoint descriptions, and Adam versus AdamW labeling in Figure 14.
